statements.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to groups of three and completed one of three collaborative tasks: an analytical survival ranking task, an ethical dilemma task, or a creative writing task (see Section 3.3 and Appendix A for full task materials).
Full task prompts and materials are provided in Appendix A.
Full system prompts and persona specifications are provided in Appendix B.
Item-level descriptive statistics are reported in Table 3.
Item-level descriptive statistics are presented in Table 4.
The full wording of the manipulation check items is reported in Table 5.

Each rubric comprised three theoretically grounded dimensions, with each dimension scored on a five-point ordinal scale anchored by detailed descriptors to support consistent application (see Appendix C for full rubrics and exemplar responses).
Representative coded exemplars for each score level are provided in the supplementary dataset.
Software and reproducibility. All analyses were conducted in R (version 4.5.1) using the lme4, lmerTest, emmeans, and clubSandwich packages.
Full confusion matrices and regression outputs are reported in Appendix D.
Full regression estimates are available in Appendix E.
(all task-specific contrasts in Appendix F).
Full estimates and marginal-effects plots are provided in Appendix G.
Full model outputs and robustness checks can be found in Appendix H.
Complete mediation models are reported in Appendix H.
This appendix provides the full task materials used in the experiment, reproduced verbatim to support transparency and replicability.
This appendix reports the full system prompts used to instantiate the AI personas in the experimental conditions.
The full prompts are provided verbatim to support transparency, reproducibility, and critical evaluation of the persona manipulation.
This appendix presents the full coding rubrics used to evaluate group discussion processes and task-specific outcomes across the study.

This appendix reports the full supplementary analyses supporting the manipulation check of AI detectability. Whereas the main text presents aggregate detectability rates and a graphical summary, the tables below provide detailed confusion matrices and logistic regression results examining whether detectability varied by task, group composition, or their interaction.

This appendix provides the complete regression outputs for the team-dynamics outcomes reported in the main paper (team satisfaction, psychological safety, and group discussion quality). For transparency, we report (i) the full fixed- effect tables for each model under both conventional model-based inference and cluster-robust (CR2) inference with Satterthwaite-adjusted degrees of freedom, (ii) Holm-adjusted 𝑝-values controlling the family-wise error rate within each dependent variable, and (iii) estimated marginal means by task and condition to aid interpretation of interaction terms.

This appendix provides the full regression outputs for standardised individual performance gain, including (i) the primary LMM with task-by-condition fixed effects and random intercepts for groups, (ii) CR2-robust inference with Satterthwaite-adjusted degrees of freedom, and (iii) estimated marginal means (EMMs) by task and condition. For transparency, we also report the full set of planned pairwise comparisons within the Analytical (survival-ranking) task, where the largest descriptive separation was observed.

This appendix reports supplementary analyses examining whether baseline depressive symptoms (BDI) moderated the effects of task and teammate configuration on primary outcomes. We present (i) model specifications for individual- and group-level outcomes, (ii) omnibus (joint) CR2 Wald tests for the full set of BDI-involving interaction terms, and (iii) follow-up estimated marginal means (EMMs) and multiplicity-controlled simple contrasts at BDI −1 SD and +1 SD.

For transparency, we provide the full estimated marginal means (EMMs) and CR2-robust simple contrasts at BDI −1 SD and +1 SD for each outcome. Each outcome corresponds to a single supplementary table, with three parts: (a) EMMs at BDI −1 SD, (b) EMMs at BDI +1 SD, and (c) CR2-robust contrasts at BDI ±1 SD. Tables are supplied as .xlsx files to preserve precision. Only Holm-adjusted significant contrasts are reported here; the complete outputs are available in the XLSX files.

Full contrasts (𝑛= 216 rows) and marginal means are provided in the following files: • Estimated marginal means at BDI −1 SD (SI_TS_EMMs_BDI_minus.xlsx) • Estimated marginal means at BDI +1 SD (SI_TS_EMMs_BDI_plus.xlsx) • CR2-robust simple contrasts at BDI ±1 SD (SI_TS_CR2_BDI_CR2.xlsx)

Full contrasts (𝑛= 216 rows) and marginal means are provided in the following files: • Estimated marginal means at BDI −1 SD (SI_PS_EMMs_BDI_minus.xlsx) • Estimated marginal means at BDI +1 SD (SI_PS_EMMs_BDI_plus.xlsx) • CR2-robust simple contrasts at BDI ±1 SD (SI_PS_CR2_BDI_CR2.xlsx)

Full contrasts (𝑛= 216 rows) and marginal means are provided in the following files: • Estimated marginal means at BDI −1 SD (SI_GDQ_EMMs_BDI_minus.xlsx) • Estimated marginal means at BDI +1 SD (SI_GDQ_EMMs_BDI_plus.xlsx) • CR2-robust simple contrasts at BDI ±1 SD (SI_GDQ_CR2_BDI_CR2.xlsx)

Full contrasts (𝑛= 216 rows) and marginal means are provided in the following files: • Estimated marginal means at BDI −1 SD (SI_z_gain_EMMs_BDI_minus.xlsx) • Estimated marginal means at BDI +1 SD (SI_z_gain_EMMs_BDI_plus.xlsx) • CR2-robust simple contrasts at BDI ±1 SD (SI_z_gain_CR2_BDI_CR2.xlsx)
This appendix reports the linguistic mediation analyses examining whether systematic differences in AI language use account for the effects of AI persona composition on team outcomes.
Full results are reported for transparency, with statistical inference emphasised on Holm-adjusted estimates.

deposits.notes: The PDF's first page links https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18234v1 (HTTP 200); the public landing page links this TeX Source archive. The same paper was also returned by the DataCite title and author searches. Downloaded and inspected the 6,029,160-byte gzip/tar archive entirely in memory. All 16 regular files are listed. This is manuscript source with figures, not a participant-data deposit or analysis-code repository. The 0_main.tex manuscript includes S1 task instructions, AI persona prompts and scoring rubrics (Appendices A-C), plus aggregate model tables (Appendices D-H). No participant/group records, participant-authored stories, chat transcripts, statistical analysis scripts, coded-exemplar dataset or XLSX files are included. The three has_* flags refer to linked record-level variables and participant outputs, not condition descriptions, aggregate estimates or task prompts printed in the manuscript. The S2 pilot is described in the paper but no pilot records are supplied. The materials_only classification and S1 coverage refer only to the embedded experimental materials.

notes:
Read the entire 180,346-character markdown in ten consecutive chunks, including all Appendices A-H, and checked availability/materials statements directly against the PDF with PyMuPDF. The PDF contains 64 physical pages; its running footer says 'of 65'. Locators use the physical PDF page numbers, which match the printed page numerators. Quotes preserve the PDF wording and characters, with whitespace and line wraps normalized. No formal data-availability statement, data-on-request offer, preregistration identifier, or analysis-code/data-repository URL was found. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty.

Public experimental materials exist only in the manuscript/source package recorded above. No usable participant-level or participant-linked output-level data were found. The supplementary dataset mentioned in section 3.7 is described only as representative coded exemplars; it is not confirmed to contain a complete participant sample. Appendix G names 12 XLSX files, all reproduced in the statements, but supplies no download URL. The statement '216 rows' refers to reported contrast-table rows, not observed participant records, and is not used as rows_checked. None of these supplements is embedded in the PDF or present in the inspected source archive.

The missing raw arm means, SDs and SEs, separate originality/elaboration/coherence effects, discussion-component effects, per-outcome analyzed counts and participant-text diversity measures cannot be recovered from this archive. The printed model estimates are not raw arm descriptive statistics. The missing XLSX files also prevent checking the repeated Table 37 values or the full moderation contrasts. Scoring/standardization details and the inconsistent BDI terminology remain unresolved.

All successful repository searches listed in searches returned HTTP 200, and the returned result lists were inspected completely (no remaining pages). DataCite title search returned one record, DOI 10.48550/arxiv.2512.18234, classified as Preprint with no relatedIdentifiers; it is the paper rather than a separate dataset. DataCite author search returned 40 records; the only matching paper record is linked in relevant. Other records concern different papers, including unrelated Figshare healthcare-reflection and thalassemia datasets and a dissertation. The Zenodo author search returned one unrelated review by Sneha.V.K, record 22063218; it is not this paper's data. Zenodo title search, Harvard Dataverse title/author searches and the initial OSF title/name-in-title searches returned no matching records. The broader OSF 'Blindspot' search returned nine unrelated projects.

The initial Zenodo title and author requests used size=100 and both returned HTTP 400: anonymous page size is limited to 25. Those failed attempts are recorded with n_results and relevant null. Repeated both requests with size=25 and received HTTP 200 and the counts above, without authenticating. All other initial searches used page[size]=100 (DataCite/OSF) or per_page=100 (Harvard Dataverse). Successful Zenodo searches used size=25.

OSF's required nodes filter searches titles, so the Lixiang Yan title-filter query is not an author-metadata search. An additional OSF users request, https://api.osf.io/v2/users/?filter%5Bfull_name%5D=Lixiang+Yan&page%5Bsize%5D=100, returned HTTP 200 and one matching profile, j5w4q, whose Tsinghua School of Education affiliation matches the paper. Its public projects and registrations endpoints both returned HTTP 200 and zero records. The profile URL in relevant is an author-search match, not a deposit. A separate Zenodo creators.name:"Yan, Lixiang" query returned HTTP 200 and zero results.

Landing-page checks: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18234, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18234v1 and https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.18234 all returned HTTP 200; the DOI redirects to the arXiv landing page. The landing page lists only v1, submitted 20 December 2025, and links the PDF, HTML and TeX Source, with no paper-specific external supplementary-data link or journal reference/publisher DOI. The manuscript says 'Preprint submitted to Elsevier' but names no journal, so a separate publisher article landing page could not be identified. Generic arXiv 'Code, Data, Media' service toggles are not evidence of a deposit.

Author-search follow-ups: DataCite detail requests for 10.48550/arxiv.2512.18239 and 10.48550/arxiv.2605.23426 both returned HTTP 200. The former describes a different 224-student study. The latter may reuse the same recruited sample (905 people and matching demographics), but reuse is not confirmed; its HTML at https://arxiv.org/html/2605.23426v1 returned HTTP 200 and supplied no dataset/repository or data-on-request link. Neither is treated as a deposit for c965. Generic GitHub links in arXiv HTML concern rendering/feedback tools, not the paper's code, and no GitHub API request was made.

The only explicit URL in the markdown body is the bibliography citation https://doi.org/10.1145/3706598.3713757; it redirected to https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3706598.3713757 and returned HTTP 403 with a bot-check page. Stopped there. It refers to Claggett et al.'s different paper, not c965 data. Other PDF bibliography DOI annotations are citations to other works, not data/material links for this paper.

Confidence is medium because the unnamed supplementary dataset and named spreadsheets could exist elsewhere under different metadata. The inspected public archive is conclusively materials/aggregate manuscript content only. No account was used, access requested, or bot check bypassed. No downloaded data/archive was saved to disk.
